Have you already allowed TB-A to run in the background and excluded it from android battery optimisation to rule them out as the possible cause? You should do this in any event to ensure timely notifications when the screen is off.

Some phone manufacturer's include a gaming mode app that allows users to control unwanted interruptions while playing supported games by disabling calls and some notifications. Samsung Game Booster and Oneplus Game Mode are two examples. Have at look at their settings if you have these or a similar app installed.

content:
I’ve noticed similar behavior with Android notifications during longer gaming sessions. It does sound more like Android’s battery optimization or background process management than Thunderbird itself, especially if notifications appear normally once you leave the game.

I’d check Thunderbird’s battery settings first and make sure it isn’t restricted in the background. Also check whether your phone has a gaming or performance mode that limits background activity.

Heavy games can definitely put more pressure on system resources, so keeping Thunderbird unrestricted while allowing the game to use performance mode might be a good compromise. It’s interesting how even simple background tasks can get affected when the phone is under sustained load.
